entrypoints.summary: A consumer parses attacker-supplied XML and iterates attributes through BytesStart::attributes() with default duplicate checks; try_get_attribute and NsReader can reach the same check.

affected_components.role: The duplicate-check implementation changed from all-prior-name scanning for large tags to a hash pre-filter with collision fallback.
Regression benchmark constructs a single empty tag with distinct attributes and iterates them with checks enabled or disabled.

causal_paths.kind: XML start-tag attribute iteration to duplicate check

code_slices.fixed: The fix introduces a thresholded HashSet of 64-bit attribute-name hashes, with a linear fallback to identify the exact prior duplicate position after a hash hit.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The added benchmark iterates attributes of generated single-element XML inputs across increasing attribute counts; the commit states it is a regression benchmark and CI smoke test.
code_slices.vulnerable: The issue describes the pre-fix function as linearly scanning self.keys for each attribute before pushing the new key.

negative_controls: Iterating with with_checks(false) is identified as avoiding the affected check for direct Attributes consumers.
Fixed versions use a hash pre-filter above the configured threshold.
observability.positive_marker: Reported release-build timings scale approximately fourfold when the number of attributes doubles, consistent with quadratic checking.

preconditions: A downstream application parses XML supplied by an untrusted party.
The application reaches Attributes iteration with default duplicate checking, calls try_get_attribute, or uses NsReader.
The installed quick-xml version is earlier than 0.41.0.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A single element with N distinct attributes, such as namespace-prefixed names.
trigger_steps.summary: Construct one XML empty/start tag containing many distinct attribute names and parse it with quick-xml.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: The reproducer loops over bs.attributes() and unwraps each attribute.
trigger_steps.summary: Iterate the parsed tag's attributes without disabling the default duplicate checks.

impacts.concept: XML parsing worker denial of service

relation_candidates.rationale: Each distinct attribute causes the default check to compare its name with all prior names in the tag.
relation_candidates.src: untrusted XML start tag with many distinct attribute names

relation_candidates.dst: XML parsing worker denial of service
relation_candidates.rationale: The documented pure-computation path can pin a parsing CPU and stall a worker.
The patch switches larger tags to a 64-bit hash pre-filter while retaining exact duplicate reporting on hits, making whole-tag work O(N).

sources.concept: untrusted XML start tag with many distinct attribute names

impact.affected_asset: Availability of the XML-parsing thread/worker and its service.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause quadratic CPU work by supplying an XML start tag with many distinct attribute names to an affected quick-xml consumer that uses the default duplicate checks or NsReader.
impact.security_effect: CPU-exhaustion denial of service of the thread or worker parsing a crafted XML start tag.

causal_trace.summary: An input XML start tag contains N distinct attribute names; N is bounded only by the buffered start-tag size.

The default duplicate-name check performs a linear comparison against every previously seen attribute name for each yielded attribute, rather than maintaining linear total work for a tag with many attributes.
IterState::check_for_duplicates scans its collected key ranges and then records the new key, producing O(N²) byte comparisons while Attributes is iterated.
The pure-computation check can pin the parsing thread's CPU for minutes to hours and is not interruptible by I/O-based timeouts while it runs, denying service to that worker.

failure.operation: IterState::check_for_duplicates during Attributes iteration performs repeated linear scans of preceding attribute-name keys.

primary_invariant.statement: Duplicate-attribute-name detection for one start tag must not impose quadratic total comparison work as the count of distinct attribute names grows.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Before the fix, each newly yielded attribute name was linearly compared with all names already recorded in the tag.

quality.review_notes: The issue contains a standalone reproducer and reported timing measurements, and the upstream commit adds a regression benchmark plus describes a unit test. This bundle does not contain an independent execution log from this extraction, so no test or benchmark execution result is asserted. The affected commit boundary is represented by advisory/OSV version scope rather than a separately verified vulnerable repository commit.

remediation.invariant_restored: For tags above 32 attributes, the fix uses a 64-bit hash pre-filter and retains a linear scan only on a hash hit to preserve exact duplicate-position reporting, making whole-tag checking O(N).
mitigation_classes: optional disabling of duplicate checks where detection is not required

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Supply one start tag whose attribute names are distinct and numerous, then cause the consumer to iterate its attributes under the default checks.
data_structure_invariants: Before the fix, previously seen attribute-name ranges are scanned to reject repeats.
After the fix threshold, hashes of previously seen names are retained so most nonduplicate names avoid a full scan.
A hash hit is verified by linear scan so reported AttrError::Duplicated positions remain exact.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: Limited by the size of the buffered start tag; the issue demonstrates generated tags with tens of thousands or more distinct names.
numeric_domains.name: attribute count N

state_context.state_machine: Attributes iteration maintains the names previously encountered in the current XML start tag while duplicate checking is enabled.
